title: T1608 — Stage Capabilities
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker registers a staging domain, uploads malware and tools, installs a TLS certificate, plants a link, and a user clicks it while the SOC watches certificate logs, passive DNS and proxy telemetry.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Everything here happens before any victim is involved.

nodes.label: Payload host
nodes.tip: Rented cloud server where the malware installer and tools are uploaded.

nodes.label: Staging domain
nodes.tip: A freshly registered domain that fronts the whole operation.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: An office worker. The only person who can connect staging to a real compromise.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Joins public telemetry with internal logs to unmask the staging.

steps.title: Register fresh domain
steps.caption: The attacker registers safe-update-center[.]com (age: 0 days) and rents a small cloud server. Nothing malicious is visible yet - the site does not even exist.
steps.defender: Passive DNS records the first resolution and WHOIS shows a brand-new registration. New-domain feeds ingest it automatically.

steps.caption: On the rented host the attacker installs a web server and builds a fake software-update page that will greet victims later.
steps.defender: Nothing visible from your network. URL scanning services may already fingerprint the page if a crawler stumbles on it.

steps.title: Install TLS certificate
steps.caption: A free TLS certificate is requested and installed, so the staged site now shows the trusted padlock icon in every browser.
steps.defender: The issuance appears in public Certificate Transparency logs within minutes - the earliest reliable alarm you can automate.

steps.title: Plant the link
steps.caption: The staging URL goes out: a short email that looks like an invoice notice, plus posts in two web forums the target industry reads.
steps.defender: The mail gateway sees the URL but has no reputation data for such a young domain - URL rewriting and click tracking is your safety net.

steps.title: Victim clicks
steps.caption: The employee clicks the link and lands on the fake update page. A valid padlock shows - exactly the trust the attacker paid nothing for.
steps.defender: First internal evidence: one proxy and DNS hit for a domain that is 2 days old with almost no global traffic.

steps.title: Payload download
steps.caption: The page offers Installer.zip. The browser saves it to the Downloads folder. The staged capability has reached a real victim.
steps.defender: EDR logs the file with the internet-zone marker and the proxy shows an archive from a rare host - two independent signals.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC joins the dots
steps.caption: The analyst connects the fresh domain, the fresh certificate, the feed-reported hash, and the one internal click. The domain is blocked and users are checked.
steps.defender: Hunting finds no other internal contact. Blocks land at proxy, DNS, and mail, and the take-down request burns the attacker's investment.
